explication:
## Purpose and Runtime
M3E Canvas is a browser-only Material 3 Expressive screen-sketching tool. Users compose multi-screen phone/desktop designs, connect interactions, preview flows, and export AI-coding prompts or PNGs. It is a Next.js 16 / React 19 static export with no application backend; project state, provider keys, and drafts remain in browser storage. Entry routes are `app/layout.tsx` and `app/page.tsx`.

## Editor Shell and Canvas
The main page coordinates the interactive desktop editor: canvas manipulation, selection, screen/part placement, undo/redo, guides, grouping, and persistence. Material components are rendered as reusable React nodes rather than generated application code.
- `app/page.tsx`
- `components/M3Node.tsx`
- `components/Toolbar.tsx`

## Design Model and Layout Operations
A shared project model represents screens, parts, geometry, groups, z-order, links, and screen variants. Shape definitions and layout cleanup provide the domain rules behind drag/drop, magnetic connected groups, responsive phone/desktop adaptation, and the reversible “tidy” operation.
- `lib/project.ts`
- `lib/shapes.ts`
- `lib/tidy.ts`

## Authoring Panels
The editor shell exposes focused panels for adding components, editing selected-node properties, managing layering, changing visual tokens, and choosing icons. These panels mutate the same project model and are the principal UI boundary around canvas actions.
- `components/PartsPalette.tsx`
- `components/Inspector.tsx`
- `components/Layers.tsx`
- `components/ThemePanel.tsx`
- `components/IconPicker.tsx`

## Preview and Interaction Graph
Navigation links are configured on tappable parts and screens, then rendered as a tap/swipe-through preview with directional, fade, expand, or no transitions. The preview is a runtime interpretation of the authored screen graph, separate from the static canvas representation.
- `components/Preview.tsx`
- `components/M3Node.tsx`
- `lib/project.ts`

## Prompt, Sharing, and AI Boundary
Prompt generation converts the project or an individual screen into localized natural-language implementation instructions for Android or web targets. Share links serialize designs for reopening in another browser. Optional AI rewriting sends requests directly from the browser to OpenAI, Anthropic/Claude, Gemini, or DeepSeek using a user-supplied key; no server proxy exists.
- `components/PromptPanel.tsx`
- `lib/prompt.ts`
- `lib/share.ts`
- `lib/ai.ts`
- `public/agent.md`

## Theming, Localization, and Mobile Mode
Material 3 Expressive color, shape, typography, and motion tokens drive both component rendering and preview behavior. Four-language strings/prompt output are centralized in localization logic. On narrow devices the app switches to a simplified fixed-screen, button-oriented editor.
- `lib/theme.ts`
- `lib/color.ts`
- `lib/tokens.ts`
- `lib/i18n.ts`
- `components/Mobile.tsx`

## Delivery and External Assets
`next.config.ts` produces a static site, including configurable base-path support. GitHub Actions publishes the generated `out/` directory to GitHub Pages on `main`. Google Fonts and Material Symbols are external visual assets; the symbol catalog is bundled locally.
- `next.config.ts`
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
- `public/material-symbols.json`
- `app/globals.css`
